chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz from Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan ibn Rashid who said:
I asked al-Askari (peace be upon him) in al-Madina about a man who bequeathed wealth in the way of Allah, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The way of Allah is our Shias'.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Askari mean by 'The way of Allah is our Shias'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Askari (peace be upon him) provides a specific exegetical interpretation of 'fi sabilillah' by identifying it with the Shia, thereby elevating the community's spiritual status to that of the divine path itself. This definition carries significant jurisprudential weight, particularly in the distribution of Zakat and Khums, as it allows for the allocation of funds directly to the faithful followers of the Ahl al-Bayt as a primary means of supporting the religious community. The narration underscores the Shia theological view that adherence to the Imams constitutes the true essence of striving in the way of Allah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’far Al Razaaz, from Muhammad Bin Isa and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid who said,

‘I asked (Imam) Al-Askary<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Medina about a man who had bequeathed wealth to be in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, is (a reference to) our<sup>asws</sup> Shias’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far al-Raziy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from al-Hassan ibn Rashid who has narrated the following: “I once asked al-‘Askariy, Alayhi al-Salam, in al-Madinah about the case of a man who has made a will to spend in the way of Allah. He (the Imam) said, ‘In the way of Allah is our Shi ’ah (followers).”’
